answer: Sybil resistance comes from a per-identity bond that is slashed, not a one-time fee. A farmer spawning many identities must post collateral for each separately, and each clone sits on its own ledge of isolated reward history. Credit is weighted by time served, so a fresh puppet gains nothing until it survives the same warmup as a real peer. On any checkpoint dispute every sibling sharing one funding source is forfeited. The attacker thus pays locked capital plus forgone yield per clone, so a fake echo of a thousand identities costs far more than joining once on the ridge of verified peers.
